motifs.name: Back-rank mate
motifs.idea: The king is locked behind its own pawns. A rook or queen crashing onto the 8th rank is instant death.

motifs.name: Smothered mate
motifs.idea: A knight mates a king boxed in by its own pieces. The knight cannot be blocked or captured.

motifs.name: Ladder mate with two rooks
motifs.idea: Two rooks sweep the king to the edge: one cuts, one checks. The simplest mate in chess.

motifs.name: Queen + knight mate
motifs.idea: Queen invades the 8th rank defended by nothing — the rook on f8 cannot stop it because the king has no escape.

motifs.name: Anastasia's mate
motifs.idea: Knight on e7 controls g8/d8 flight squares while a rook/queen mates along the edge file.

motifs.name: Arabian mate
motifs.idea: Knight + rook: the knight covers the corner escape squares while the rook mates on the edge.

motifs.name: Fork: knight royal fork
motifs.idea: Knight jumps to a square attacking king and rook at once — the classic "royal fork".

motifs.name: Fork wins the queen
motifs.idea: A knight check that also hits the queen. Forks are the #1 way beginners lose material.

motifs.name: Skewer through the king
motifs.idea: Check the king on a line, and when it steps aside you capture the queen behind it. The opposite of a pin.

motifs.name: Discovered check wins material
motifs.idea: Move the blocking piece away to unleash check from behind, then grab whatever you like with the moving piece.

motifs.name: Pin the defender
motifs.idea: Bg5 pins the f6 knight to the queen. Pinned pieces cannot move — attack them repeatedly.

motifs.name: Win the queen with a deflection
motifs.idea: Deflect a defender away from its duty — the guarding piece is overloaded and something falls.

motifs.name: Promotion tricks
motifs.idea: A pawn one step from promotion is often worth more than a piece. Push it before anything else.

motifs.name: Trapped queen (Nc3-d5 style)
motifs.idea: An advanced queen with no retreat is a target. Trap it with calm developing moves.

motifs.name: Two bishops mating net
motifs.idea: Bishops dominate long diagonals; two bishops sweep the king across the board.

motifs.name: Zugzwang in the endgame
motifs.idea: Sometimes the winning move is to force the opponent to move — every legal move loses.
